court: In the High Court of Madras†
advocates: For R 1 to R 3 : Mr. S. Ravi Additional Public Prosecutor
For R 4 : Mr. M. Muthumanikkam Government Advocate (civil side)
judgment_text:
PRAYER : Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India for issuance of writ of mandamus, to direct the respondents 1 to 3 to provide adequate police protection and to ensure the peaceful and uninterrupted conduct of the temple festival and related religious activities by considering the petitioner's representation dated 4-4-2026.

The Order of the Court was delivered by

L. Victoria Gowri, J.:— Seeking to direct the respondents 1 to 3 to provide adequate police protection for the conduct of temple festival of Arulmigu Chelliyamman @ Mariamman Temple situated at Sudalavayal Village, Manamelkudi Taluk, Pudukkottai District, by considering the petitioner's representation dated 4-4-2026, this writ petition is filed.

2. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is the hereditary trustee of the aforesaid temple. However, during the conduct of the temple festival in the previous year, an FIR came to be registered against the petitioner in connection with a dispute that arose over the placement of loudspeakers. Pursuant thereto, his trusteeship was removed under Section 54 of the HR & CE Act. It was contended that such removal is not permissible in law, as the said provision can be invoked only upon the conviction of the trustee in a criminal case. Aggrieved by the same, the petitioner approached this Court by filing W.P.(MD). No. 10868 of 2026, wherein this Court set aside the order of removal while granting liberty to the respondent authorities to initiate fresh action in accordance with law. As on date, the petitioner's trusteeship stands restored and he continues to function as the trustee. Apprehending similar action, the petitioner submitted a representation seeking adequate police protection; however, the same has not been considered. Hence, the present petition.

3. The learned Additional Public Prosecutor, Mr S. Ravi, submitted that the apprehension of the petitioner is baseless, and that issues arise only in the absence of consensus among the members of the temple.

4. Heard either side and carefully perused the materials available on record.

5. Considering the submissions made, the respondents 1 to 3 are directed to consider the petitioner's representation dated 4-4-2026 and provide adequate police protection to the aforesaid temple, upon receipt of payment from the petitioner, in accordance with G.O. (Ms) No. 139, Home (Pol-VIII) Department, dated 4-3-2019.

6. With the above directions, this Writ Petition is disposed of.
